summary: Nyingcha Duoji is a Tibetologist who studied at Boston University and earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.
Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Katok and Nyoshul Monasteries, as well as under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Penor Rinpoche.
Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Ogyen Trinley Dorje (born 1985) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Bokar Rinpoche, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Pema Donyo Nyinje.

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Berlin (1937–1944), the University of Jena (1944–1945), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Freiburg, Pennsylvania, and Halle-Wittenberg, and was appointed professor of historical and Indo-European linguistics at the University of Munich in 2008.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his doctorate under Ernst Steinkellner at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) specialized in history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, he held posts at the University of Michigan, the W. F. Albright Institute, Harvard (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS, where William Stede supervised his PhD, and became Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Ceylon in 1943.

Oliver Petersen (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Geshe Thubten Ngawang from ~1983 to 2003 and held a post at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg around 1983.
Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, he held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).
Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Pierre L. Lamant and held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient around 1991.

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Copenhagen, Harvard, and the University of Washington, completed doctoral work under Tord Olsson, and served as responsible publisher at Lund University (attested 2000–2007).

Om Prakash is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma. He held posts at Kirori Mal College and as professor of economic history at Delhi (attested 2003).

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (~1912–1915). He held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1920 to 1939.
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Khenpo Shenga.
